content.text:
Ceate an SVG of an awkward family portrait of robots. Give each robot a distinct personality, and suggest their relationships through poses and composition. No text.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.11.1 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

{
  "chunk_id": "exec-1-1",
  "command": "mkdir -p output src && ls -la",
  "description": "Create output directories",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "terminal_status": "completed",
  "output": "total 0\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 4 fender  staff  128 Oct 13 15:50 .\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 4 fender  staff  128 Oct 13 15:50 ..\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 2 fender  staff   64 Oct 13 15:50 output\ndrwxr-xr-x@ 2 fender  staff   64 Oct 13 15:50 src\n",
  "original_output_bytes": 208,
  "original_output_tokens": 52,
  "truncated": false
}

The image shows five robots (plus a pet) frozen mid-shoot against a mottled 1980s studio backdrop with a camera-flash burst: the tall dad in a suit forces a too-wide grin with one antenna bent from stress, his arm hovering stiffly in mid-air rather than around mom; mom, polished in teal with pearls, leans almost imperceptibly away with a tight, twitching smile and a hand planted on her hip; grandma on the far left has already fallen asleep on her cane, head tilted, drooling a drop of oil; the teen on the right slouches in headphones with arms crossed, leaning out of the group with rolled, half-lidded eyes; and the small yellow kid photobombs front-and-centre, kicked up on one leg, waving wildly, while the robot dog sits beside the teen facing entirely the wrong way.
